result.journal: International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning (iJET)
result.keywords: This study explores learners’ perceptions of interactive augmented reality content integrated into college English science modules. Drawing on assessment-for-learning principles and an interactive teaching approach, the article examines how AR-supported tasks influence engagement, usability, and perceived learning gains in a blended instructional setting. The sample consisted of 84 first-year college students enrolled in a private university during the 2020-2021 academic year. A mixed quantitative design was used, combining an attitude scale for augmented reality applications with learning performance indicators across four dimensions: engagement, content completion, interaction, and application confidence. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and paired-samples comparisons. Results suggest that students found the AR-enhanced modules interesting, accessible, and helpful for connecting scientific vocabulary practice with communicative English activities, and many indicated a willingness to continue using the approach in future courses.
result.title: Assessing Learners’ Perceptions of Interactive Augmented Reality in College English Science Modules
